1.title: Hijri New Year
1.description: The beginning of a new Hijri year invites Muslims to reflect on the passage of time, renew their intentions, and remember the Hijra — the migration of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from Mecca to Medina. It is an opportunity to look back with gratitude and move forward with purpose.

9.title: Tasua
9.description: Tasua is associated with the events surrounding Ashoura and the martyrdom of Imam Hussain, the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, at Karbala. Fasting alongside Ashoura is also practiced by many Muslims as a way to distinguish this observance from other traditions.

10.title: Ashoura
10.description: Ashoura recalls the salvation of Musa (Moses) and the Children of Israel from Pharaoh. It is also a day of mourning for the martyrdom of Imam Hussain at Karbala, particularly in Shia traditions. The day carries themes of faith, sacrifice, courage, and standing for justice.

12.title: Mawlid an-Nabi
12.description: Mawlid commemorates the birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and provides an opportunity to learn about his life, character, mercy, and teachings. Muslims differ on the religious status and manner of observing this occasion, but all can benefit from studying and following his example.

1.title: Beginning of Rajab
1.description: Rajab is one of the four sacred months in Islam. Its beginning is a reminder to honor the sanctity of these months, avoid wrongdoing, and prepare spiritually for the seasons of worship that follow.

27.title: Laylat al-Mi'raj
27.description: Laylat al-Mi'raj commemorates the miraculous Night Journey of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ from Mecca to Jerusalem and his Ascension through the heavens. The event is a reminder of divine signs, perseverance, and the central importance of prayer in the life of a Muslim.

15.title: Laylat al-Bara'at
15.description: Laylat al-Bara'at is traditionally regarded as a night of forgiveness and mercy. In many communities, Muslims use it for personal reflection, repentance, and supplication. The manner and religious status of observing it vary among Islamic traditions.

1.title: Beginning of Ramadan
1.description: Ramadan is the month in which the Quran was revealed. It is a period of fasting, spiritual discipline, generosity, and deeper connection with Allah. Beyond abstaining from food and drink, Ramadan encourages Muslims to improve their character and compassion.

19.title: Conquest of Mecca
19.description: The Conquest of Mecca was a turning point in the history of Islam. After years of persecution and conflict, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ entered the city with a large Muslim community and chose mercy and reconciliation, granting safety to many of those who had opposed him.

27.title: Laylat al-Qadr
27.description: Laylat al-Qadr is remembered as the night on which the Quran began to be revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. It represents immense spiritual opportunity, and worship during it is described in the Quran as better than a thousand months.

1.title: Eid al-Fitr
1.description: Eid al-Fitr celebrates the completion of Ramadan. It is a day of gratitude, communal worship, generosity, and joy, bringing families and communities together after a month of fasting and spiritual effort.

29.title: Eid al-Mab'ath
29.description: Eid al-Mab'ath commemorates the beginning of the prophetic mission of Muhammad ﷺ and the first revelation. It marks the moment when the message of Islam began to be conveyed publicly and highlights the importance of revelation, knowledge, and moral transformation.

8.title: Day of Tarwiyah
8.description: This occasion marks the beginning of the central rites of Hajj. Pilgrims prepare themselves, travel to Mina, and begin a journey focused on obedience, remembrance, equality, and devotion to Allah.

9.title: Day of Arafah
9.description: The Day of Arafah is the central day of the Hajj pilgrimage. Pilgrims gather in worship and supplication on the plain of Arafah, recalling the gathering of humanity before Allah and seeking forgiveness, mercy, and acceptance.

10.title: Eid al-Adha
10.description: Eid al-Adha commemorates the willingness of Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son in obedience to Allah. It celebrates faith, trust, and generosity, and is closely connected to the sacrifice performed by pilgrims during Hajj.

11.title: Days of Tashreeh - 2
11.description: The Days of Tashreeh extend the spirit of Eid al-Adha through remembrance, gratitude, community, and generosity. During Hajj, pilgrims continue the rites of stoning the pillars in Mina as part of their devotion and rejection of evil.

12.title: Days of Tashreeh - 3
12.description: The Days of Tashreeh extend the spirit of Eid al-Adha through remembrance, gratitude, community, and generosity. During Hajj, pilgrims continue the rites of stoning the pillars in Mina and may begin preparing to leave the area.

13.title: Days of Tashreeh - 4
13.description: The final Day of Tashreeh brings the principal rites of Hajj to a close. It represents the completion of a demanding journey of devotion, patience, sacrifice, and remembrance of Allah.

18.title: Eid al-Ghadir
18.description: Eid al-Ghadir commemorates the gathering at Ghadir Khumm, where the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is understood in Shia tradition to have appointed Imam Ali as his successor. It is an occasion focused on loyalty, leadership, justice, and devotion to the Prophet's family.
